Guidance & outlook: For the first 2 months of FY 27, construction stood at approximately 638 kilometers, which is aroun d 34% lower year-on-year.
Starting with the standalone numbers; For Q1 FY27, total income stood a t INR1,320 crores as compared to INR1,339 crores in Q1 FY26, fl at year-on-year.

Ashoka Buildcon Limited August 12, 2026 Coming to consolidated numbers; Total income for Q1 FY27 stood at INR1,534 crores as compared to INR1,937 crores in Q1 FY26, this is seeing a 21% de-growth largely contributed by moneti zation of BOT and HAM projects in the Q3 FY26.
Growth & demand: Coming to the order book status, the company receiv ed 2 new project orders as discussed from Central Housing and Plannin g Authority Republic of Guyana INR328 crores in Chhattisgarh St ate Development Corporation, Gems and Jewellery Park of INR450 crores.
As on 30th June, our order book stands at INR15,25 1 crores, excluding order received after 30 June, that is ~INR450 crore s.
The breakup of the order book is road and railway comprised of arou nd INR9,648 crores, which is 63.3% of the order book.
Margins & costs: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR126 crores down to 17% Y-on-Y with EBITDA margin of 9.5%.
EBITDA for the qu arter stood at INR292 crores, down 55% year-on-year with EBITDA mar gin at 19.0%, again due to monetization of HAM and BOT assets.

H1 will continue to remain subdued, but H2 will definitely ramp up and there we'll catch up with 9.5% of EBITDA based on whatever we are spending for the ne w projects which are taking off, where initial establishment e xpense is now being Ashoka Buildcon Limited August 12, 2026 incurred, mobilization, then we had ramp up in the H 2 and margins also will loo…
Capex & expansion: The Indian budget has provided a significan t push to the railway sector with a record capital expenditure al location of approximately INR2.93 lakh crores.
So for the coming years, for '26-'27, we will have to invest INR 179 Cr on the existing HAM projects including Bowaichandi project.
So capex for this quarter was approximately INR25 c rores, of which INR7 crores was for our international projects and balance was for domestic.
Balance sheet & cash: Sir, on the debt side, we have roughly INR2,100 cro res of debt.
Third-party debt would be approximately in the rang e of, as we have guided, around INR500 crores to INR600 crores.
Around say INR1,100 crores, around approximately INR 700 crores would be third-party debt.
Risks & challenges: On one hand, the domestic highway awarding environment conti nues to remain subdued.
NHAI awarded only around 5 kilometers of projects in June compared with 102 k ilometers in May, while construction activity in June declined 32% y ear-on-year to around 274 kilometers.
